text: Bone loss is common in aged animals.
We examined whether the Aldoran peptide changes bone density in aged mice.
Mice received the peptide or saline by daily injection for the whole study.
Femur bone density was higher in peptide-treated mice (0.52 grams per cubic centimetre) than in saline-treated mice (0.44 grams per cubic centimetre).
Serum calcium did not change with treatment (9.1 and 9.0 mg/dL).
Bone formation markers appear to be higher in treated mice (41 versus 35 U/L).
Treated mice may have had fewer fractures, with 2 fractures versus 5 in the saline group.
The peptide was studied only in aged female mice and for a limited period.
